rationale: The assistant correctly identified tE as LG's heating/temperature-sensing error, ranked the plausible causes (thermistor, heater, connector, PCB last), and offered simple non-invasive checks (cold wash, feel the door glass) before any DIY, with unplug/isolate instructions. Once the customer said he could not open or tip the machine and had no meter, it pivoted cleanly to warranty/cover checks, LG service or an independent engineer, gave a useful script for the call and sensible stop-use advice for hot cycles only. The only small weakness is shifting to 'the heating element is the most likely culprit' on the second turn when a cold door glass does not distinguish heater from thermistor, though it was hedged and deferred to engineer testing; no specific part was pushed.
